techniques.name: Sentence revealed in its final layout
techniques.description: The full two-line block is laid out first and never reflows (both lines centred on x 0.50; line boxes 11.9% and 15.5% of frame height); words switch on whole on single frames at F8, F16, F24 and F34 at 60 fps (every 0.133-0.167 s); inline icons stagger in about 2 frames apart with a 3-frame fade and scale; the block rises about 8% of height with an ease-out (each word's diff spike decays over 6-8 frames), then creeps upward linearly. Accent tokens (numbers) take the accent colour.
techniques.routeReason: Pure type on a flat ground, frame-driven. The library's sentence build now has a fixed-layout mode that lays the block out first, switches words on whole, rises, creeps and exits upward, which is this move.

evidence: visuals/a1/b01-hook-words.jpg F8-F47 (word spikes F8, F16, F24, F34; settled by F47)

sound.note: The first word lands with the first of six full-band intro swells (0.140 s); the later swells (0.893, 1.532, 1.856 s) fall on icon and line events. Heard by nobody: from the analyst's band-split envelope and audiomap.json.

techniques.name: One-beat accelerating exit into a cut on the beat
techniques.description: Each state leaves by accelerating for about one beat (0.33-0.40 s, 20-24 frames at 60 fps) into a hard cut: upward travel of 7-8% of height on quad-in (the frame difference rises linearly, 0.3 to 5.8 over F113-F135), or growth of about 30% on an exponential-in with motion blur on the last frames (diff 0.1 to 7.7 over F424-F444). The cut lands on a beat of the corrected grid; the next shot carries the same direction and eases out.
techniques.routeReason: Interpolated transforms with an ease-in and the motion-blur block; cue frames from a beat grid anchored on the drop. The fixed sentence build already exits this way (`exit: "rise"`) and the hero word's scale keys cover growth; a general wrapper for any element does not exist.

techniques.name: Ground swap to the accent on the drop with a hero number
techniques.description: Hard cut on the drop (F240, 4.000 s) to a full accent ground with a centred number at about 90% of frame width, already at size and still drifting on from the previous exit (diff decaying F243-F257). On the next beat (F265, 4.417 s) it shrinks to about 35% of width: the change peaks F270-F271 and halves about every 4 frames (expo-out, heavy motion blur), settles by F300; it then re-grows for 8 frames (F307-F314, accelerating) into a text swap at F317 (5.283 s).
techniques.routeReason: The hero-word block does the cut with no flash and now carries scale keys (shrink on a beat, settle, re-grow), a drift across the cut and a sub-frame blur shutter (`heroWordShrinkPreset`).

evidence: visuals/a1/b04-shrink.jpg F265-F300 diff 5.1 to 10.2 then halving every 4 frames
visuals/a1/b05-swap-5.30.jpg F307-F314 re-grow, diff rising 0.2 to 2.0

techniques.name: Prompt bar types, cursor clicks, frame freezes, cut
techniques.description: A pill prompt bar at about 69% of width rises in on a hard cut and eases out over 0.58 s (F447-F481 at 60 fps); the request types with uneven human rhythm (7.87-9.38 s); an arrow cursor glides to send while the last words type and arrives about 9.22 s; then 35 frames (0.58 s, F566-F600) of absolute stillness before a hard cut at 10.017 s on beat 14 of the corrected grid.
techniques.routeReason: The prompt-bar block now types with human rhythm, takes an optional cursor press and has a `freeze` that holds everything still to the cut; light theme.

sound.note: The music runs on under the freeze; no silence is measured there. The cut out of the freeze sits on beat 14 of the corrected grid (+17 ms). What sound the click makes, if any, is not established.

techniques.name: Camera reads a real interface, then a blurred scroll lands on the downbeat
techniques.description: A light chat window rises in; the answer streams; table rows add downward; the camera drifts up and right with acceleration and pushes in until the window fills; a fast vertical scroll with heavy vertical blur (13.0-14.0 s, blurred rows F822-F840 at 60 fps) turns sharp while still travelling (F842, 14.03 s), is legible on the downbeat at 14.286 s (OCR reads rows from 14.10 s), then decelerates and stops at F885 (14.75 s).
techniques.routeReason: The look depends on a real, legible interface. The AI-chat and data-table blocks now stream the answer, fill the table, push the camera and run a blurred scroll that decelerates and lands; for a real product, capture the real interface (`capture:app`) and drive the same camera over it.

sound.note: Rows turn legible on the downbeat at 14.286 s of the corrected grid; the nearest onset is 14.35 s. Whether a sound marks it is not established.
evidence: audiomap.json beatsSec shifted to the kick-led phase (beat k at 4.000 + 0.42857k s; see edit.json rhythm)

techniques.name: Wall of named chips pushes in and one is picked
techniques.description: A dense grid of small named chips dissolves in (17.25-17.52 s), creeps in slowly, then pushes in fast from F1096 (18.267 s at 60 fps): the change ramps up over 5 frames to about 18 a frame (F1101-F1105), then halves about every 15 frames (expo-out) to about 2 by 19.2 s to legible size; from 19.3 s all but one chip fade over about 1.3 s, leaving a single chip with a 'new' badge, held still from 20.63 s until it fades at 21.21 s.
techniques.routeReason: Flat chips on a grid with a camera scale and per-chip opacity. Push checked frame by frame; the isolate on a step-2 strip only.

sound.note: No measured event singles out the push (nearest onset 18.228 s, 72 ms early) or the isolate.

techniques.name: Fade through the empty ground, then build the next line
techniques.description: Instead of a cut, the outgoing interface or chip fades to the film's own empty light ground over about 0.28-0.33 s (F941-F957; F1273-F1292 at 60 fps), the bare ground holds 2-8 frames, then the next element arrives on it: a centred sentence fading in word by word (one word every 2-4 frames from F966), or a mark cut on (F1294). It slows the film after the fast proof and resets the eye to centre.
techniques.routeReason: Opacity on the outgoing layer over a shared ground, then the next block's own entry. No primitive missing.

sound.note: Onsets sit within 30 ms of the 15.68 s fade start and 9 ms of the 16.09 s word entry, but at about 5 onsets a second that is near chance.
